scope: Proposition 9.2 of the manuscript “Midpoint lenses in segment spaces” (preprints/Midpoint-lenses-in-segment-spaces-September-27-2026/manuscript.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 331 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e5fa3ffa1ac9778a), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 16. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: In B∞, the root paths hv = d[o,v] and the coordinates e∗ v have norm one, and the children (e∗ v⌢j)j of each fixed vertex are weakly null. If a∥z∥ ≤ N(z) ≤ b∥z∥, with 0 < a ≤ b < ∞, then δN (a/(2b)) = 0. More precisely, put t0 = a/(2b), with d, ε > 0 below. Each of the following assumptions would permit a finite-codimensional subspace and a child whose approximation error and growth factor satisfy the corresponding row: assumed positive lower bound error less than growth factor 0 < d < δN (t0) min(a/2, ad/2) 1 + d/2 2ε < δN (t0) min(a/2, aε/2) 1 + ε/2 d = δN (t0) > 0 min(a/2, ad/4) 1 + d/4 Here the error is N(e∗ v − f) for the chosen child and its approximant f in the finite-codimensional subspace. Growth is measured relative to the N-norm of the parent root-path vector.
